ce:2022:q9-s2.title: GATE CE 2022 | Set 2 | Question: 9
ce:2022:q9-s2.question:
Match Column X with Column Y:
$$\begin{array}{|l|l|}\hline \text{Column X}&\text{Column Y} \\ \hline \text{(P) Horton equation} & \text{((I) Design of alluvial channel} \\ \hline \text{(Q) Penman method} & \text{(II) Maximum flood discharge}\\ \hline \text{(R) Chezys formula}& \text{(III) Evapotranspiration}\\ \hline \text{(S) Lacey's theory}& \text{(IV) Infiltration}\\ \hline \text{(T) Dicken's formula}& \text{(V) Flow velocity}\\ \hline \end{array}$$
Which one of the following combinations is correct?

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Fluid Dynamics and Flow Measurements
detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Matching of Hydraulic & Hydrologic Equations:**
  - **(P) Horton equation $\rightarrow$ (IV) Infiltration:**
    - Horton's equation models the exponential decline of soil infiltration capacity over time during rainfall:
      $$f_p = f_c + (f_0 - f_c) e^{-k_h t}$$
      where $f_0$ is initial infiltration capacity, $f_c$ is ultimate steady rate, and $k_h$ is the decay constant. $\implies \mathbf{(P) - (IV)}$.
  - **(Q) Penman method $\rightarrow$ (III) Evapotranspiration:**
    - Penman's method combines energy balance and aerodynamic mass-transfer equations to determine potential evapotranspiration ($PET$) from open water surfaces and vegetated crops. $\implies \mathbf{(Q) - (III)}$.
  - **(R) Chezy's formula $\rightarrow$ (V) Flow velocity:**
    - Antoine de Chézy established the classic equation for uniform flow velocity in an open channel:
      $$V = C \sqrt{R S_0}$$
      where $V$ is mean flow velocity, $C$ is Chézy's coefficient, $R$ is hydraulic radius, and $S_0$ is bed slope. $\implies \mathbf{(R) - (V)}$.
  - **(S) Lacey's theory $\rightarrow$ (I) Design of alluvial channel:**
    - Gerald Lacey developed the regime theory for designing non-scouring, non-silting channels in stable regime in alluvium:
      $$V = \left(\frac{Q f^2}{140}\right)^{1/6}, \quad P = 4.75 \sqrt{Q}, \quad R = \frac{5}{2} \frac{V^2}{f} \implies \mathbf{(S) - (I)}$$
  - **(T) Dicken's formula $\rightarrow$ (II) Maximum flood discharge:**
    - Dicken's formula is an empirical peak runoff equation widely used in North and Central India:
      $$Q_p = C_D A^{3/4}$$
      where $Q_p$ is peak flood discharge and $A$ is catchment area. $\implies \mathbf{(T) - (II)}$.

- **Synthesis:**
  - Matching: $(\text{P})-(\text{IV}), \; (\text{Q})-(\text{III}), \; (\text{R})-(\text{V}), \; (\text{S})-(\text{I}), \; (\text{T})-(\text{II})$.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option A ((P)-(IV), (Q)-(III), (R)-(V), (S)-(I), (T)-(II))**.

ce:2022:q15-s2.question: $P$ and $Q$ are two square matrices of the same order. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
options: If P and Q are invertible, then $[PQ]^{-1}=Q^{-1}P^{-1}$
If P and Q are invertible, then $[QP]^{-1}=P^{-1}Q^{-1}$
If P and Q are invertible, then $[PQ]^{-1}=P^{-1}Q^{-1}$
If P and Q are not invertible, then $[PQ]^{-1}=Q^{-1}P^{-1}$

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Linear Algebra
detailed_solution.markdown:
If P and Q are invertible then $(PQ)^{-1} = Q^{-1}P^{-1}$ is correct. Let,

$$\begin{aligned}

PQ&=C \\

P^{-1}PQ&=P^{-1}C \\

Q&=P^{-1} C\\

Q^{-1}Q&=Q^{-1}P^{-1}C \\

I&=Q^{-1}P^{-1}C \\

IC^{-1}&=Q^{-1}P^{-1}CC^{-1} \\

C^{-1}&= Q^{-1}P^{-1}\\

(PQ)^{-1}&= Q^{-1}P^{-1}

\end{aligned}$$

Hence, proved.

Similarly, we can prove if P, Q are invertible then

$(QP)^{-1}= P^{-1}Q^{-1}$

Therefore, the correct option(s) are **A, B**.

ce:2022:q20-s2.title: GATE CE 2022 | Set 2 | Question: 20
ce:2022:q20-s2.question:
The components of pure shear strain in a sheared material are given in the matrix form:
$$\varepsilon =\begin{bmatrix} 1 &1 \\ 1& -1 \end{bmatrix}$$
Here, $Trace(\varepsilon)=0$. Given, $P=Trace(\varepsilon ^8)$ and $Q=Trace(\varepsilon ^{11})$.
The numerical value of $(P + Q)$ is ________. (in integer)

detailed_solution.concept: Solid Mechanics - Bending and Shear Stresses
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned}

|A-\lambda I|&=0  \\

\begin{vmatrix}

1-\lambda &1 \\

1 & 1-\lambda

\end{vmatrix}&=0  \\

(1-\lambda)(-1-\lambda)-1&=0  \\

(\lambda^2-1)-1&=0  \\

\lambda&=\pm \sqrt{2}

\end{aligned}$$

Eigen values of $\varepsilon$ are $\sqrt{2}$ and $-\sqrt{2}$

Eigen values of $\varepsilon ^8$ are $(\sqrt{2})^8$ and $( -\sqrt{2})^8$

Eigen values of $\varepsilon ^{11}$ are $(\sqrt{2})^{11}$ and $(-\sqrt{2})^{11}$

$P=Trace(\varepsilon ^8) =$ sum of Eigen values $= ( \sqrt{2})^8+( -\sqrt{2})^8=32$

$Q=Trace(\varepsilon ^{11}) =$ sum of Eigen values $= ( \sqrt{2})^{11}+( -\sqrt{2})^{11}=0$

$P+Q=32+0=32$

Therefore, the correct answer is **32**.

(Consider 1 h.p. = 746 W; unit weight of water = 9810 $N/m^3$)

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Hydraulic Pumps
detailed_solution.markdown:
Base period (B) = 120 days

$$\begin{aligned}

Delta (\Delta )&=144 cm=1.44m\\

Duty(D)&=\frac{8.64B}{\Delta }=\frac{8.64 \times 120}{1.44}\\

D&=720\frac{hec}{cumec}\\

Q&=\frac{Area}{D}=\frac{108}{720}=\frac{3}{20}m^3/s\\

Q_{applied}&=\frac{Q}{\eta _a}=\frac{3}{20 \times 0.8}=\frac{3}{16}\\

\text{Power required}&=\frac{mgh}{t}\\

&=\rho _w \times \left ( \frac{volume}{t} \right )g \times h\\

&=\rho _w Qgh=\gamma Qh\\

&=9810 \times \frac{3}{16} \times 10\\

&=\frac{73575}{4}watt

\end{aligned}$$

Horse power of pump  $= \frac{\text{Power required}}{746 \times \text{efficiency}}=\frac{73575}{4 \times 746 \times 0.8}=30.82hp$

Therefore, the correct answer is **31** (acceptable range: [30, 32]).

ce:2022:q48-s2.title: GATE CE 2022 | Set 2 | Question: 48
ce:2022:q48-s2.question:
Two discrete spherical particles (P and Q) of equal mass density are independently released in water. Particle P and particle Q have diameters of 0.5 mm and 1.0 mm, respectively. Assume Stokes' law is valid.
The drag force on particle Q will be________ times the drag force on particle P. (round off to the nearest integer)

primary.subtopicLabel: Boundary Layer Theory, Drag and Lift

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Boundary Layer Theory, Drag and Lift
detailed_solution.markdown: In case of discrete particle settling and Stoke's law valid, at terminal velocity, since there is no change in velocity, the net force on the body is zero. Hence, $F_D=\left ( \frac{\pi}{6}D^3\rho _sg-\frac{\pi}{6}D^3\rho _sg \right )=\frac{\pi}{6}gD^3(\rho _s-\rho _f)$ For density of medium $(\rho _f)$ and mass density of sphere $(\rho _s)$ constant, Drag force $(F_D)\propto D^3$ For particle P, diameter $(D_P)=0.5 mm$ For particle Q, diameter $(D_Q)=1 mm$ $\Rightarrow \frac{(F_D)_Q}{(F_D)_P}=\frac{(D_Q)^3}{(D_P)^3}=\left ( \frac{1}{0.5} \right )^3=8$ $\Rightarrow (F_D)_Q=8 \times (F_D)P$ Therefore, the correct answer is **8**.

ce:2022:q53-s2.question: Assuming that traffic on a highway obeys the Greenshields model, the speed of a shockwave between two traffic streams (P) and (Q) as shown in the schematic is _______ kmph. (in integer)

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Traffic Engineering
detailed_solution.markdown:
$\text{Speed of shock wave}=\frac{\text{Change in flow}}{\text{Change in density}}$

$\text{Flow}=\text{Speed} \times \text{Density}$

$$\begin{aligned}

Density&=\frac{Flow}{speed}\\

&=\frac{q_Q-q_P}{\frac{q_Q}{V_Q}-\frac{q_P}{V_P}}\\

&=\frac{1800-1200}{\frac{1800}{30}-\frac{1200}{60}}\\

&=\frac{600}{60-20}\\

&=15Kmph

\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **15**.
